story: At 7:17 on a sunny Friday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at home pouring cornbread batter into a pan for the oven, content with his quiet kitchen work. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is puttering about with determination while Hal dutifully counts the pink flamingos in view against the town's limit of three. Meanwhile Rosa is at her dining table smoothing napkins and fussing over the centerpiece, hopeful that all four seats will look welcoming for her guests.
events: Gary (gary fridge): Pour the batter into the pan and slide the cornbread in to bake
Donna waited: puttering around Magnolia Loop (the street)
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street against the L-02 limit of three
Rosa (rosa dining table): Straighten the napkins, fix the centerpiece, and make sure all four seats look welcoming

gary.thought_process: I mixed the batter last tick and the pan is ready, so the cornbread needs to go in the oven. It's 7:17 PM and Rosa's dinner is tonight, so I can't dawdle. The fridge is the only cooking object I have in this zone. The cart stays parked until Hal signs off, so the lights and sound system can wait. Once the cornbread is baking I can head over to Rosa's with the pan.

parameters.content: Pour the batter into the pan and slide the cornbread in to bake

donna.thought_process: Hal is standing right there counting flamingos against L-02. I already told him last tick that I moved the extras behind the hedge and asked him to count again, so I shouldn't repeat myself. The polite thing is to let him finish his count and respond to what he finds. Meanwhile, my real goal is the pickleball ladder and Gary. Nothing more to say to Hal until he reports, so I'll tidy the flock to make sure exactly three show, which keeps my promise and keeps him off my back before Rosa's dinner.
donna.engine_note: tried to use None, which isn't in magnolia_loop

hal.thought_process: Donna says she moved the extras behind the hedge, so only three should show from the street. She invited me to count, and the right thing is to actually check the flock against L-02 rather than take her word. Gary's cart paperwork is still unfinished business, but the flamingos are right in front of me and I'm already here. Counting honors both my by-the-book nature and the fair deal I made with her. Then I can ease off before Rosa's dinner.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street against the L-02 limit of three

rosa.thought_process: It's 7:17 PM and the table is set, the sides are covered, and I've checked the shift schedule twice already. Nobody is here yet, and I don't want to keep fussing with food that's ready. I've already done the kitchen check several ticks in a row, so a different small touch would be better than repeating myself. The centerpiece and place settings are the last thing guests will notice, so I'll give the table one final walk-through and straighten things so it feels warm when Gary, Donna, and Hal walk in.

parameters.content: Straighten the napkins, fix the centerpiece, and make sure all four seats look welcoming

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
